name: Semnam
confidence_why: 2 independent first-hand descriptions agree (1 state the same rule, 0 refine it); none contradicts.

tone_statements.citation: Benjamin, Geoffrey. 2012. The Aslian languages of Malaysia and Thailand: an assessment. In Stuart McGill & Peter K. Austin (eds), Language Documentation and Description, vol. 11, 136-230. London: SOAS.
tone_statements.quote: It has occasionally been claimed that lexical tone exists in some of the Northern Aslian languages (Schebesta 1928b: 205; Phaiboon 1984; Bishop 1996a). [...] The majority of Mon-Khmer languages, including the majority of Aslian languages, lack lexical tone. [...] Several Mon-Khmer languages exhibit a phonemic register (phonation-type) distinction between the clear (i.e. normal) and breathy articulation of vowels. Until recently, however, no such register distinction was known for any Aslian language, so its recent discovery in Mah Meri (Kruspe & Hajek 2009; Stevens et al. 2006) should be regarded as an innovation peculiar to that language, not as a Mon-Khmer retention.
tone_statements.locator: pp. 185-186, sec. 4.2.2 'Tone and register' (Semnam's own phonology is discussed at pp. 160, 166, 179-180, not 178-179)
tone_statements.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)

audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification
audit.reasoning: Coding 'fixed-dominant, final stress' rests on the only existing description of Semnam, a 2009 first-hand phonology sketch by the primary fieldworker; the deciding sentence is verified verbatim in the now-downloaded PDF (correct the locator from p. 285 to p. 284), and the same paper's ~670 stress-marked phonetic transcriptions are uniformly final-stressed, with Matisoff 2003 confirming the Aslian-wide final (major-syllable) stress pattern. No grammar, later phonology or instrumental study of Semnam/Lanoh exists (Glottolog: 0 descriptive refs; web search nil), so no better source can change the classification. Action: record the copy consulted, fix the page locator, fill the empty grade field citing p. 284 + §3.5 p. 292 transcriptions; no reclassification.

sources.citation: Burenhult, Niclas & Claudia Wegener. 2009. Preliminary notes on the phonology, orthography and vocabulary of Semnam (Austroasiatic, Malay Peninsula). Journal of the Southeast Asian Linguistics Society 1: 283-312.

sources.citation: Matisoff, James A. 2003. Aslian: Mon-Khmer of the Malay Peninsula. Mon-Khmer Studies 33: 1-58.
sources.quote: Family-level only: Aslian sesquisyllables consist of a 'major' syllable with fully-stressed vowel preceded by a 'minor' syllable; in true disyllables the non-final vowel is unstressed. Semnam appears only in the language abbreviation list, no Semnam-specific stress statement.
sources.note: Family-level Aslian overview stating major (final) syllable carries stress; corroborates the 'as in other Aslian languages' premise of our deciding quote. downloaded now; confirms.
